react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm pathway analysis of ten differentially abundant metabolites revealed a primary signature centred on sulfur amino-acid metabolism and its intersection with xenobiotic detoxification. The strongest signal was Biological Oxidations (REACT:R-HSA-211859), which ranked first in the RaMP multi-database ORA with FDR = 1.24e-06 and a fold-enrichment of 132.2, driven by coumarin, 3-aminopropanal, 6-methylthiopurine and glutathione. This broad oxidation pathway acts as the upstream gateway for Phase I and Phase II drug metabolism, consistent with the concurrent enrichment of Phase I - Functionalization of compounds (REACT:R-HSA-211945, FDR = 2.08e-03) and Phase II - Conjugation of compounds (REACT:R-HSA-156580, FDR = 1.33e-03). The drug-adduct conjugate Azathioprine ADME (REACT:R-HSA-9748787, FDR = 1.38e-04) directly implicated 6-methylthiopurine and glutathione as participating in the same metabolic fate. Sulfur amino-acid metabolism was independently detected across three paradigms: RaMP hit Degradation of cysteine and homocysteine (REACT:R-HSA-1614558, FDR = 1.38e-04) and Cysteine and methionine catabolism (WP:WP4504, FDR = 1.38e-04); Mummichog's m/z-direct analysis ranked Methionine and cysteine metabolism (MUMM:methionine_and_cysteine_metabolism) fourth with p = 0.0081; and MetaboAnalystR PSEA ranked Taurine and hypotaurine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00430) first at p = 0.0249. Hypotaurine (KEGG:C00519) and glutathione (KEGG:C00051) are the dual driver metabolites threading these sulfur pathways. Beta-mercaptoethanol (KEGG:C00928), methimazole (KEGG:C07190) and coumarin (KEGG:C05851) all contain reduced sulfur or are substrates for S-transfer reactions, reinforcing the sulfur-handling theme. InChIKey reconciliation across ChEBI, KEGG, HMDB and LIPIDMAPS confirmed zero structural conflicts for any of the five driver metabolites, confirming the signal is not a namespace artefact.

Glutathione (CHEBI:16856) is the only compound that recurs as a hit across all five top pathways from all three tools. final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm pathway analysis of ten differentially abundant metabolites revealed a primary signature centred on sulfur amino-acid metabolism and its intersection with xenobiotic detoxification. The strongest signal was Biological Oxidations (REACT:R-HSA-211859), which ranked first in the RaMP multi-database ORA with FDR = 1.24e-06 and a fold-enrichment of 132.2, driven by coumarin, 3-aminopropanal, 6-methylthiopurine and glutathione. This broad oxidation pathway acts as the upstream gateway for Phase I and Phase II drug metabolism, consistent with the concurrent enrichment of Phase I - Functionalization of compounds (REACT:R-HSA-211945, FDR = 2.08e-03) and Phase II - Conjugation of compounds (REACT:R-HSA-156580, FDR = 1.33e-03). The drug-adduct conjugate Azathioprine ADME (REACT:R-HSA-9748787, FDR = 1.38e-04) directly implicated 6-methylthiopurine and glutathione as participating in the same metabolic fate. Sulfur amino-acid metabolism was independently detected across three paradigms: RaMP hit Degradation of cysteine and homocysteine (REACT:R-HSA-1614558, FDR = 1.38e-04) and Cysteine and methionine catabolism (WP:WP4504, FDR = 1.38e-04); Mummichog's m/z-direct analysis ranked Methionine and cysteine metabolism (MUMM:methionine_and_cysteine_metabolism) fourth with p = 0.0081; and MetaboAnalystR PSEA ranked Taurine and hypotaurine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00430) first at p = 0.0249. Hypotaurine (KEGG:C00519) and glutathione (KEGG:C00051) are the dual driver metabolites threading these sulfur pathways. Beta-mercaptoethanol (KEGG:C00928), methimazole (KEGG:C07190) and coumarin (KEGG:C05851) all contain reduced sulfur or are substrates for S-transfer reactions, reinforcing the sulfur-handling theme. InChIKey reconciliation across ChEBI, KEGG, HMDB and LIPIDMAPS confirmed zero structural conflicts for any of the five driver metabolites, confirming the signal is not a namespace artefact.
